app.name: GitHub
app.description: A web-based platform for version control and collaboration using Git.

notes: Tested: a custom auth config created without `oauth_redirect_uri` sends `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Register exactly the URI your auth config sends, or set `oauth_redirect_uri` to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and register that instead.
Composio sends users to `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize` with `redirect_uri=https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` by default.
Default scopes requested by Composio include `repo`, `user`, `gist`, `notifications`, `project`, `workflow`, and `codespace`.
If using a GitHub App instead of an OAuth App, the user must still install the GitHub App on their organization or account separately before tool calls can execute.

assumption: An AI agent that reads and writes repositories, manages GitHub Actions, and accesses user profiles across any customer's GitHub account.

verdict.headline: GitHub OAuth app registration is entirely self-serve with zero review or approval required.
verdict.summary: You can register a custom OAuth app in developer settings instantly and connect your accounts without any administrative gate. No review or verification is needed for standard apps, though organization owners may need to approve the app for private repositories.

handsOnEffort.label: 15–30 min
handsOnEffort.basis: Creating an OAuth app and entering credentials into Composio takes minutes.

timeToFirstConnection.label: 0–1 hour
timeToFirstConnection.basis: Apps are live immediately upon creation.

timeToProduction.label: 0–1 day
timeToProduction.basis: No approval or review cycle; ready for production deployment instantly.

verdict.longestPole: Organization admin approval for private repository data access (if applicable).
verdict.costDetail: Free of charge for standard OAuth app creation and API usage within rate limits.

factors.detail: Any user or organization can create up to 100 OAuth apps directly via Developer Settings.
Standard custom OAuth apps do not require prior review, approval, or verification to go live.
Not required for standard OAuth apps (only needed for optional marketplace publishing or organization verification).
No mandatory security review or questionnaire required for standard custom OAuth apps.
Standard OAuth applications and REST/GraphQL API access are free within rate limits.
No partner agreements or sales contact needed to create and deploy an OAuth app.
No user caps or deployment mode restrictions apply to standard OAuth apps.
Centralized OAuth app works across all users, though organization owners may need to approve the app for private organization repos.

phases.title: Register OAuth App
phases.outcome: A registered GitHub OAuth App with client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Navigate to GitHub Developer Settings
steps.details: Log in to GitHub and navigate to **Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App**.

steps.title: Fill App Metadata and Callback URL
steps.details: Enter your **Application name** and **Homepage URL**. Set the **Authorization callback URL** to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` (or `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback`). Click **Register application**.
steps.agentAssist: Draft the application name, description, and homepage URL for the developer to paste.

steps.title: Generate Client Secret
steps.details: On the app settings page, click **Generate a new client secret**. Copy both the **Client ID** and the generated **Client Secret** immediately.

phases.title: Configure App Settings
phases.outcome: App settings configured for optional token expiration and security features.

steps.title: Configure User Access Token Expiration
steps.details: Determine whether to enable expiring user tokens under the app settings. When enabled, access tokens expire after 8 hours and refresh tokens expire after 6 months with mandatory rotation.

phases.title: Go live in Composio
phases.outcome: Custom OAuth app wired into Composio and ready for tool execution.

steps.title: Create Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.details: In your Composio dashboard, navigate to **Auth Configs → Add Custom Auth**, select **GitHub**, and input your GitHub App **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.
steps.agentAssist: Use the Composio API to create the custom auth config by passing the client ID and secret programmatically.

steps.title: Verify Default Scopes
steps.details: Confirm that Composio requests the required default scopes (`repo`, `user`, `gist`, `notifications`, `project`, `workflow`, `codespace`) during the connection flow.
steps.agentAssist: Verify scope payload via the Composio toolkit API endpoint (`GET https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/github`).

requirements.detail: A standard GitHub user account to access developer settings and register the OAuth app.
Basic metadata required when creating a new OAuth App in GitHub Developer Settings.
Must match the Composio callback URI (e.g. https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add or callback).

scopes.purpose: Full control of private and public repositories including read/write access to code, issues, and pull requests.
Read private and public user profile data.

blockers.title: Organization Approval Required for Private Repositories
blockers.symptom: API calls to private repositories fail with 404 or permission errors despite successful OAuth connection.
blockers.howToProceed: Ask the organization owner to approve the OAuth app for the organization via Organization Settings → Third-party access.

blockers.title: Rate Limit Exceeded
blockers.symptom: API requests return HTTP 403 with a rate limit exceeded message.
blockers.howToProceed: Ensure requests are authenticated via the OAuth token to get the 5,000 requests/hour limit instead of the 60 requests/hour unauthenticated limit.

blockers.title: GitHub App vs OAuth App Confusion
blockers.symptom: Trying to use GitHub App installation links and permissions interchangeably with OAuth app scopes.
blockers.howToProceed: Note that GitHub App installation is separate from OAuth credential setup. If bringing a GitHub App, ensure it is installed on the target account/organization manually.

nuances.title: Token Lifetimes and Rotation
nuances.detail: If expiring tokens are enabled, access tokens expire after 8 hours (28,800 seconds) and refresh tokens expire after 6 months of inactivity with mandatory token rotation.

nuances.title: PKCE Support
nuances.detail: GitHub OAuth flows support PKCE via S256 (`code_challenge` / `code_verifier`), which Composio handles automatically.

nuances.title: No OIDC Discovery Document
nuances.detail: GitHub does not publish an OIDC discovery document at `.well-known`. Authorize and token endpoints are fixed at `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize` and `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token`.

nuances.title: API Rate Limits
nuances.detail: Authenticated REST requests are limited to 5,000 requests per hour (15,000 for Enterprise Cloud). GraphQL requests are limited to 5,000 points per hour.

steps: Navigate to the Composio dashboard and go to Auth Configs.
Click Add Custom Auth and select GitHub.
Paste your GitHub OAuth App Client ID and Client Secret.
Save the auth configuration and use the generated auth config ID in your agent session requests.
